_comment: Hand-curated layer of docs/capabilities.json (capability-config.md §2 p.3). The emitter (stapel_forms/_capabilities.py) merges this over the derived axes; an axis present in conf.py DEFAULTS but missing here (or vice versa) is a loud emission error. Keep business_label/summary in business language — they surface in CTO conversations, not in code. The axes are the settings that change WHAT THE PRODUCT PROMISES a respondent: which field kinds a form may ask, whether their IP is kept, how long their answers live, whether public forms run without a captcha, and whether a form that changed mid-fill still accepts the old one. The throttle rates, size gates, volume caps, page sizes and the notify cooldown are deliberately NOT axes — they bound abuse and tune throughput; they do not change the deal. `surface_roots` + `surface` are the usage surface (stapel_tools.surface): the symbols a host or sibling module is meant to CALL instead of writing its own version. Deliberately NOT rooted: events.py (the service layer emits form.* inside its own mutating transactions — host code that emits them double-publishes a public fact), functions.py/actions.py (comm surface, reached by name over the bus, never imported), checks.py (Django check callbacks), presenters.py (the view layer's DTO discipline; hosts reach it through the PRESENTERS swap keys documented as an extension point), notifications.py (the module owns its own reaction; a host that wants another one subscribes to form.submission.received). The `capabilities` block is the curated half of the WORKSPACE CAPABILITY projection (a permission string a host grants in STAPEL_WORKSPACES["ROLES"], not a config switch): the operations each one gates are derived from schema.json's x-stapel-capability, written by views.CapabilityAwareAutoSchema off the same @gated(...) declaration that authorizes the request, so what is published and what is enforced cannot diverge. An entry here for a capability nothing enforces, or an enforced capability with no entry here, is a loud emission error.
provides: Admin-defined forms with anonymous responses: a workspace-keyed form whose schema is a list of stapel-attributes FeatureDefs, immutable published versions (every response records which schema it answered), two anonymous endpoints (fetch schema by non-enumerable public handle, submit answers) hardened by module-namespaced throttles, netintel-tiered captcha, size and volume caps and a recipient-side notify cooldown, capability-gated response review with streamed injection-safe CSV export, admin-initiated resend, ids-only form.* events, a GDPR provider and a finite retention purge.

requires.reason: comm bus (form.* Actions, the workspaces.check_capability client), JWT authentication, unified error envelope, netintel-tiered captcha, notification publishing, GDPR provider registry, staff-mandate declarations, AppSettings config layer
the field vocabulary IS this library's FeatureDef registry, and every submission is validated and normalized by its pipeline — forms defines no field types of its own

every admin request asks the workspaces.check_capability comm Function (fail-closed, deny-by-default) — stapel-workspaces is the shelf's answerer; any provider of that Function satisfies the contract, and without one the admin surface denies while the public respondent endpoints keep working

notify-on-submit and resend request notifications through stapel-core; without a notifications service the rows are still stored and the events still emitted, but nobody is told. The forms.submission_received / forms.submission_resend routing entries must exist there (or in the host's STAPEL_NOTIFICATIONS['TYPES'])
the FormsGDPRProvider registers itself for authenticated respondents; hosts must also list "forms" in STAPEL_GDPR['DATA_OWNERS'] or the erasure closure never completes (check stapel_forms.W003)

extension_points.name: FIELD_KINDS
extension_points.summary: Which stapel-attributes kinds a form schema may use (default: the ten builtins). A host that registers a custom kind through STAPEL_ATTRIBUTES['EXTRA_TYPES'] or register_feature_type() adds it here to make it askable — registering a type somewhere in the process never by itself opens it to strangers on a public URL.

extension_points.name: attribute type registry
extension_points.summary: The field vocabulary itself is stapel-attributes' open registry, not a forms-local type system: a new question type is a type contribution there (config + DTO + DAO + validation), and it becomes server-validated in forms for free. The React pair mirrors it with registerFormFieldWidget.

extension_points.name: PRESENTERS
extension_points.summary: Every DTO is built by a presenter resolved through STAPEL_SWAP — swap keys FORMS_FORM_PRESENTER / FORMS_VERSION_PRESENTER / FORMS_SUBMISSION_PRESENTER reshape the form, version and response envelopes of every admin endpoint without forking a view. The anonymous envelope is deliberately not swappable: it is the one shape whose contents are a security decision.

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every view declares request/response serializer seams (SerializerSeamMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, remount the URL.

FIELD_KINDS.business_label: What a form may ask for
FIELD_KINDS.summary: The question types available to form authors. Ships as the ten builtin attribute kinds — text, number, yes/no, choice, date, section heading, colour, hierarchical choice, unit-bearing number. File uploads are absent by construction, not by omission: the platform's CDN cannot take custody of a stranger's bytes (no anonymous ingest, no auth-gated download), so a form attachment would be world-readable by URL. Widening this list is how a product adds its own question type after contributing it to stapel-attributes.

STORE_CLIENT_META.summary: Off. The module does not persist a respondent's IP or browser string — rate limiting and network classification work off the live request and the cache, so nothing needs it on disk. A host that must keep abuse forensics turns it on, and that data then falls under the same retention clock as the answers themselves.

RETENTION_DAYS.summary: 365 days, and finite is the point: anonymous respondents sit outside the platform's user-keyed erasure apparatus, so a bounded lifetime is the honest privacy mechanism rather than an implied promise. A form may shorten its own horizon; lengthening past the module ceiling requires raising the ceiling, so one form's settings cannot quietly rewrite the deployment's retention policy. Setting it to nothing keeps answers forever — an explicit choice a host makes, never the shipped default.

ALLOW_UNCAPTCHAED_PUBLIC.business_label: Run public forms with no captcha
ALLOW_UNCAPTCHAED_PUBLIC.summary: Off, and it is a confession switch rather than a feature: a deployment with open public forms and no captcha backend gets a startup warning naming this setting. Turning it on silences the warning by saying the refusal is deliberate — which is a defensible position for an internal deployment and a bad surprise for a public one.

ACCEPT_PREVIOUS_VERSION_SECONDS.business_label: Grace period after a form changes
ACCEPT_PREVIOUS_VERSION_SECONDS.summary: Zero. Publishing an edit mints a new immutable version, and a response in flight against the old one is refused wholesale so the renderer can refetch and tell the respondent the form changed — better than half-validating answers against a schema they never saw. A host that would rather accept the tail of in-flight fills opens a window here.

forms.view.summary: Read-only access to the form catalogue: which forms exist, their state and public handle, and the published version history. It carries no sight of what anybody answered — that is a separate grant, because the people who need to know a survey exists are usually not the people entitled to read the replies.
forms.view.behavior: Holding it is necessary and sufficient — the routes below ask for this exact string and nothing else. What it cannot tell a client: a 403 from these routes means EITHER the capability is not granted OR the workspaces service rendered no verdict. stapel-core's require_capability still collapses outage into denial (verified against 0.45.0: a FunctionCallError returns None, it never raises WorkspaceLookupUnavailable), so the 503 branch in stapel_forms.authz cannot fire. Treat a 403 as "not now", not as "this principal will never hold this"; re-read the grant from the workspaces service rather than caching the refusal.

forms.manage.summary: Create, rename, edit the draft, publish a version, open or close the form, rotate the public link, soft-delete, and read the builder's field-kind dictionary. This is authorship of the questionnaire and of the URL strangers answer it on; it does not by itself grant sight of a single response.

forms.responses.view.summary: Read what respondents wrote: the keyset response listing, one response in full, and the CSV export. There is deliberately no separate export capability — an export is a read, and pricing it differently would only invite the belief that the listing is the safer of the two.

forms.responses.manage.summary: Act on a stored response: delete one permanently, or re-send one to the form's notify targets (or to an override list). This is the destructive half of response handling and the practical channel for an erasure request arriving by email from an anonymous respondent, who has no self-service route. Grant it to whoever answers for that promise, not to everyone who may read the replies.

create_form.intent: Create a workspace-keyed form as a draft, with its non-enumerable public handle already minted and its retention override validated.

update_form.intent: Rename a form or replace its settings blob; the per-form retention override is checked against the module ceiling here, so one form's settings can never quietly rewrite the deployment's retention promise.

save_draft.intent: Replace the builder's scratchpad. Deliberately permissive — a half-built form must be savable, and publish is the gate.

publish.intent: Validate the draft (caps, kind allowlist, duplicate slugs, silently-dropped config keys, per-field config validity) and freeze it as the next immutable version, atomically with the form.published emit.

set_state.intent: Open or close a form for submissions: enforces the per-workspace open-form cap, refuses opening an unpublished form, and emits form.closed exactly once.

rotate_link.intent: Mint a new public handle after a leak. Every distributed link dies and the row keeps its responses — which is the whole point of rotating rather than recreating.

delete_form.intent: Soft-delete: intake stops immediately and rows survive for review until the retention purge cascades them.

get_form.intent: Fetch one live form inside a workspace scope — a form in another tenant, or in the trash, is a 404 rather than a row you have to remember to filter.

list_forms.intent: The workspace's live forms, newest first, optionally narrowed by state.

resolve_public.intent: Resolve a public handle with the uniform-404 discipline: unknown handle, soft-deleted form and draft are one byte-identical 404, while closed is 410 because that handle was public by definition and the renderer needs the difference.

submit.intent: Accept one answered form: active-version check, volume cap, validation, normalization into typed storage and the ids-only event, all in one transaction. Nothing reaches disk that the version's own configs did not produce.

list_submissions.intent: Keyset page of a form's responses, newest first, capped service-side.

get_submission.intent: One response inside a workspace scope.

delete_submission.intent: Destroy one response — the practical channel for an erasure request that arrives by email, until an email-keyed GDPR subject exists upstream.

resend_submission.intent: Re-deliver one response to the form's notify targets or to an explicit override. Not cooldown-gated: the cooldown suppresses a respondent-driven flood, and an operator asking for one letter is not one.

erase_user_submissions.intent: Erase a user's answers while keeping the tombstone, so response counts and per-version analytics stay truthful.

purge_expired.intent: Hard-delete responses past their retention horizon, honouring per-form overrides. After the horizon the count claim expires too, so these rows leave no tombstone.

purge_deleted_forms.intent: Destroy soft-deleted forms and everything under them, in the order the PROTECT constraint requires (answers before the versions they reference).

authorize.intent: THE access decision for the admin surface. Returns allow|deny|unavailable (503, never 403-on-outage); fail-closed via workspaces.check_capability by comm name. Every new admin read or write routes through this — a second membership check is how a capability later ships half-enforced.

normalize_schema.intent: Coerce an authored schema (full envelope or bare field list) into the stored shape, refusing anything else as a schema error rather than a 500 three layers down.
instead_of: indexing into a posted JSON body

validate_schema.intent: Refuse a draft that may not become a published version: field cap, kind allowlist, duplicate slugs, config keys the attributes dataclass would silently drop, then per-field config validity.

validate_answers.intent: Validate a submitted answer set against a published schema, returning per-field errors that carry params.field plus the unknown slugs the attributes engine would have ignored. The engine is right to ignore them for listings and wrong for a public form.

to_dao.intent: Normalize validated answers into typed stored shapes. Never call it on unvalidated input: the engine's normalizer skips rather than refuses, so an invalid value would round-trip into storage.

schema_fields.intent: The field-def list of a stored schema, tolerant of anything already on disk.

schema_meta.intent: The form-level meta (title, description, confirmation text, submit label) of a stored schema.

answer_columns.intent: The (slug, label) columns of one version for review and export, section headings omitted. Stable per version — which is what the version FK buys.
instead_of: a union of columns over mutated schemas

csv_rows.intent: One streamed, page-capped CSV export of a single version's responses, plus the keyset cursor for the next page. An export is the one read whose size is chosen by whoever filled the form in.

escape_cell.intent: Render a stored answer as a CSV-safe string, escaping the leading characters a spreadsheet would execute.

export_filename.intent: A safe attachment filename derived from the form title.
instead_of: putting an admin-authored title into Content-Disposition

purge_expired_submissions.intent: The schedulable retention job: a plain callable, additionally a celery shared task under a stable name when celery is installed, logging what it destroyed. A retention policy nobody schedules is a promise, not a mechanism.
instead_of: a cron script calling into the ORM

get_forms_beat_schedule.intent: The beat entry for the retention purge on the configured cadence, for a host to spread into CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE.
instead_of: hardcoding the task name and crontab in host settings

capability_for.intent: The workspace capability answering a forms action, and the only place that mapping is read — call it instead of hardcoding a "forms.*" string, so a host-side gate and this module's gate can never name different permissions for the same door.
